selection_policy: Seven tracks: 48 tasks each for Android, iOS, Linux desktop, macOS, Windows, and Web, plus 12 single-screen cross-device workflows. Web tasks run in a browser on the Linux VM (the Open-series web apps and diagrams.net); Linux desktop tasks use native applications.

Cross-device workflows run on one screen: the desktop shows a companion Android phone in a scrcpy window, and the agent works on the phone and on the desktop, moves the file between them itself, and returns results to the phone. The six Linux + Android workflows replace the six Android-to-Windows cross-VM workflows (same Markor sources and LibreOffice targets); the six Windows + Android workflows replace the six Windows-to-Linux cross-VM workflows (the Notepad stage moves to Markor on the phone, the LibreOffice stage to the Windows desktop). The cross-VM stage definitions they were converted from, and their oracle companions, are supporting files listed under supporting.cross_vm_stages and do not count as tasks.

Each single-platform track takes tasks from the reviewed CUA-Tasks-Review import first and fills the remainder from earlier OS-Omni tasks (iOS, macOS, Windows from the previous v1 selection; Linux desktop from the original Linux catalog, excluding duplicates of reviewed tasks and tasks without a resolvable evaluator or initializer).

Within a track, tasks are drawn round-robin across applications for coverage; ties favor implementation-ready tasks, tasks already reviewed for v1, more recent tasks, oracle companions and hard difficulty, then task ID.

To make room for the cross-platform workflows, two tasks were retired from each single-platform track (listed under retired). A track with tasks missing a resolvable initializer retires those first; Linux desktop, which has none, retires tasks whose declared oracle companion is missing; Web, which has no dependency gaps, retires by coverage only. Within those candidates, tasks come from the application with the most tasks in the track (Open-series photo-edit variants count as one application), preferring non-Open-series applications on ties, then non-hard tasks without an oracle companion.
